resources.string: These are local download results, not a live upstream guarantee. Failed refreshes keep the last validated cache; without a cache the bundled list is used. Opening this screen does not start downloads or change the VPN.

Keeping seeds uses BUNDLED + FRESH, never previous downloads. Download-only removals already work. Feed-only replacement also lets upstream removals remove bundled seeds. A saved selection affects each category only after its next successful refresh; failures keep its existing cache. Category switches and parent rules are unchanged.

Use only each newly validated feed after a successful refresh? Bundled seeds missing from that feed will no longer be pinned. This can reduce protection. Current caches stay unchanged until a successful refresh. Parent-managed rules and the VPN are not changed.

Keep bundled seeds on future successful refreshes? This restores missing bundled seeds only when that category next refreshes successfully. Existing caches, parent-managed rules and the VPN are not changed now.
Policy saved. Refresh to apply; existing caches have not changed.
Not saved: another operation is running or local storage failed. Try again when idle.

Shrink protection rejects a feed that loses more than 25% of its last accepted unique feed hosts (not its bundled or merged count). First downloads and legacy caches use the 100-host minimum until a baseline is recorded. Check the source first. To accept a legitimate shrink, approve that exact rejected revision with your PIN and retry. Changed content needs fresh approval. Approval never bypasses UTF-8, parse, size or minimum-count checks.
A feed operation is already running. No second operation was queued.

Limits: 5,000,000 raw AND assembled UTF-8 bytes per category, at least 100 unique hosts, at most 3 HTTPS redirects. One serialized operation; 45-second source / 180-second run deadlines with connection/read timeouts. Daily work runs only when protection is enabled and Android permits it; temporary errors get at most two retries. No online availability is inferred from saved metadata.
